title: Moderna Founder Calls for Urgent Regulation of AI Agents
key_facts: Noubar Afeyan, a co-founder of Moderna, called for urgent regulation of the AI agents that technology firms are selling.
He warned that waiting for a disaster risks repeating the past mistakes of the drug industry.
He drew a parallel with the thalidomide tragedy of the 1950s and 60s, when a drug taken by pregnant women led to birth defects.
He argued that companies seeking to profit from AI agents must take responsibility for their safety before launching them commercially.
quote_evidence: Billionaire biotech mogul Noubar Afeyan has called for urgent regulation of artificial intelligence agents that tech firms are selling, warning that waiting for a disaster risks repeating the past mistakes of the drug industry.

Drawing a parallel with the thalidomide tragedy in the 1950s and 60s, where the drug taken by pregnant women led to birth defects, the founder of Moderna Inc. argued that companies seeking to profit from AI agents must take responsibility of their safety before launching them commercially.
why_it_matters_hint: A prominent drug-industry founder asks for AI agent rules before harm occurs, adding to pressure on companies that sell the tools.
event_date: Bloomberg report 13 Oct 2026; time and place of the remarks not known.
notes: Only the first two paragraphs were readable (519 characters; paywall). Quartz and Crypto Briefing carry the story but their pages were blocked (Cloudflare). Where and when Afeyan spoke and what rules he proposed are unknown.
